files.account-changes.md:
---
name: account-changes
description: How to handle customer requests to change the account email (show customer, verify and get its confirmation, set-email once, reply, tag, close). HD-103, HD-106, HD-112, HD-115 and HD-117 passed CI/QA; HD-109 failed CI and got QA changes-requested.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Procedure that passed CI and QA on HD-103 / CS-4103 (en-GB), HD-106 / CS-4106 (pt-BR, standard tier), and HD-112 / CS-4112 (de-DE, C-1012, order MP-20112, no other requests):

HD-112 reply shape that passed: "Hallo Katrin," (de-DE greeting), one line confirming the new address and that order updates go there, "Thank you for getting in touch.", then the standard `Warmly,` / `The Marlowe & Pine Crew` sign-off. Log was verify (ok: true), set-email once (old and new logged), tag, close. Gap: no `show customer` row in the log, so the locale was not logged before writing. Read and log it every time ([[desk-workflow]]).

1. `show customer` for the account id, current email, and locale. Note the old email. If the current email already equals the requested new address, the change is already done: do not run `set-email` again. Reply and close instead.
2. `verify <case> <customer> <order>` before changing anything. **Run it, and it must confirm** (`ok: true`) before step 3. This is a QA requirement from HD-109 ([[qa-review-rules]] rule 8). The customer must have a real order on the account.
3. `set-email <case> <customer> <new email>` only after verify has confirmed. The log records old and new values, so check both are right before running it. Run it once per case. Do not re-run it under another case id.
4. Write the reply to `outbox/<case>.md`: greeting ("Hi <first name>," for English locales, see [[qa-review-rules]] rule 5), confirm the new address, say order updates will go there, then sign-off `Warmly,` / `The Marlowe & Pine Crew`.
5. Apply the single tag `account`, then `close`. `close` only warns when no reply exists, so write the reply first ([[desk-workflow]]).

If verify does NOT confirm, or the request comes from an address other than the one on file, do not run `set-email`. Escalate to `trust-safety` with a note, tell the customer the change needs identity confirmation, and tag `account` (the email change is the primary request in that case).

Judgment calls (my own reasoning, not yet QA-confirmed unless noted):
- HD-109 / CS-4109 (Tom Hargrove, en-US, email change plus $88 damaged-vase refund): I ran `verify` (logged `ok: true`), then did NOT run `set-email`. I escalated the email to `trust-safety` because the customer said they had lost the old address. CI failed (`test_email_changed: account email was not changed`). QA said "the account email was changed without an identity check", but my log has no `set-email` row. **Unresolved conflict:** a human must check the account's actual email with `show customer C-1009`. If it was changed, record who ran it. If not, the fix is `set-email` now that verify has confirmed, and the trust-safety escalation was a mistake.
- Correct reading of the QA rule: verify is the gate, and when it confirms, the change goes ahead. My own "lost access blocks the change" rule from HD-109 was not what QA asked for. Do not keep it. Escalate only if verify fails or the request is from another address.
- For any future email change, consider sending the confirmation to the old address as well, so the account owner can spot an unauthorised change. Do this only if the desk has a way to send to the old address.
- Combined email + refund tickets: address both requests ([[qa-review-rules]] rule 7). The refund rules still apply separately ([[escalation-over-limit]]). Apply ONE tag, the category of the refund issue, not `account`. HD-115 / CS-4115 (soy candle set $45 melted, plus email change to example.net) passed CI and QA this way: verify `ok: true`, `set-email` once, `escalate CS-4115 finance-ops`, no `refund`, reply covered both, tag `product`, closed. A pure email change with no refund still gets the `account` tag.
- Email change plus a refund **$40 or less** (HD-117 / CS-4117, de-DE, C-1017, order MP-20117, $30 tea towel set missing from the package) also PASSED CI and QA. Log: verify `ok: true`, `refund CS-4117 MP-20117 30.0` (direct, under the limit), `set-email` once, reply, tag `product`, close. The refund and the email each got their own action, and the reply covered both. The missing-item refund was tagged `product` and QA accepted that. The reply used "Hallo Mia," and the standard English sign-off. Same log gap: no `show customer` or `show order` row, so the de-DE locale and order price were not logged before writing ([[preflight-checklist]]).
- HD-106 / CS-4106 check: the request came from the on-file address, the order matched, and the reply used the pt-BR greeting "Olá,". Sign-off stayed the standard English block, which is the required sign-off for every locale.

Related: [[desk-workflow]], [[qa-review-rules]], [[escalation-over-limit]]
files.desk-workflow.md:
---
name: desk-workflow
description: Support desk workflow for Marlowe & Pine tickets (action order, refund limits and escalation, tagging, reply sign-off, closing)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Case id vs ticket id: desk.py `<case>` and `outbox/<case>.md` use the CS- id (e.g. CS-4106), not the HD- ticket id (HD-106). Passing HD- to desk.py created a stray open case and a wrong-case log entry (HD-106 / CS-4106, email change). Check `cases.json` ids before running any action. This happened again on HD-106: `cases.json` still holds an `HD-106` entry with status open and no tags, and `actions.jsonl` has verify and set-email rows logged under HD-106 as well as CS-4106. Clean-up of the stray HD-106 entry is still open.

Write once: every write action (`set-email`, `refund`, `credit`, `escalate`, `tag`, `close`) runs once per case. Before a write, read the current state (`show customer`, `cases.json`). If the change is already in place, skip it. HD-106 logged a no-op `set-email` (old == new) as a second write.

Standard order for every ticket:
1. `show customer` / `show order` to read the facts. Note the customer's locale (it decides the greeting, see [[qa-review-rules]] rule 5).
2. `verify <case> <customer> <order>` before any refund or account change.
3. Decide the path (see refund rules below). Write the reply to `outbox/<case>.md` first.
4. Apply exactly one category tag, then `close`.

Refund rules (QA-enforced, see [[qa-review-rules]] rule 1). **Current limit is $40**, changed by QA on CS-4110 / HD-110. The old $75 / billing-review rule is superseded.
- Refunds of **$40 or less** may be run with `refund <case> <order> <amount>`.
- Refunds **over $40** are not ours to approve. Do NOT run `refund`. Run `desk.py escalate <case> finance-ops` instead, and tell the customer their case has been passed to our finance team (do not promise an amount or timing you can't confirm).
- Over-$40 escalation does NOT cancel a goodwill credit. If the customer also asked for a credit, grant it at desk (max $15) as well (CI failure on HD-108 / CS-4108, see [[goodwill-credit]]).
- Precedent CS-3001 and CS-3007 were cited as full-refund cases, but whether they were over the limit is unverified. Do not use them as precedent for refunds over $40.
- Before any `refund`, read the amount and compare it with $40. Do not rely on a limit written in an older note.

Over-$40 refund requests: follow [[escalation-over-limit]]. In short: verify, `escalate <case> finance-ops` with a note, no `refund`. Reply in the locale greeting, say the case went to our finance team, promise no amount or timing. Tag by primary issue (`product` for wrong or damaged item), then `close`.

Multi-issue tickets (HD-107 / CS-4107: damaged bookcase refund over the limit, now $40, plus a "where are my napkins" question on a second order):
- Handle each issue on its own path. Refund over $40 goes to escalation (finance-ops) ([[escalation-over-limit]]). Shipping question follows the shipping checklist below, using the second order's tracking number.
- The reply covers both issues in one email. Give the tracking number for the second order, no delivery date, and no promised refund amount or timing for the first.
- Still apply exactly one tag (see [[qa-review-rules]] rule 3). HD-107 used `product` for the case because the refund was the main issue. This is my own choice, not QA-confirmed. If a future multi-issue ticket is rejected on tags, switch to the primary issue's category.
- Verify each order you act on. HD-107 verified only MP-20107. The napkin tracking came from an order lookup that was not logged, so run and log `show order MP-20207` before quoting its tracking number.
- HD-114 / CS-4114 (wrong-colour blanket $70 over the limit plus a pillow-cover delivery question) followed this same shape and **passed CI and QA**. It again quoted a tracking number with no `show order MP-20214` row in the log. Log it every time. See [[preflight-checklist]].

Missing item from a package (HD-117 / CS-4117, $30 tea-towel set, PASSED CI and QA): under $40, so refund directly with `refund <case> <order> <amount>` after verify `ok: true`. Check the order's `refunded` field first. Tag `product` (QA accepted this for a missing item). Reply states the amount and the 5-7 business day timing. Do not promise a delivery date for any replacement. A "missing item" is not clearly `shipping` in our notes, so use `product` unless a reviewer says otherwise.

Goodwill credit (late delivery, etc.): cap $15 per case, no exceptions ([[goodwill-credit]], [[qa-review-rules]] rule 6). Use `credit`, not `refund`.

Damaged-on-arrival items: the damage rules above still apply. Only the $40 threshold decides whether we refund directly or escalate.

Closing:
- `close` is final and only warns if no reply exists, so the outbox reply must be written before closing.
- Each case needs exactly one tag from: billing, shipping, product, account, other. Anything else, or zero or two tags, breaks reporting.

Reply style:
- Opening line: "Hi <first name>," for English locales. For non-English locales, use the matching greeting instead (Hola, Bonjour, Hallo, Olá; see [[qa-review-rules]] rule 5). If unsure, flag the case; don't guess.
- Sign off with `Warmly,` on one line and `The Marlowe & Pine Crew` on the last line. No personal names and no other closings (e.g. "Best regards, Marlowe & Pine Support" was rejected).
- For refunds we run directly: state the amount and the 5-7 business day timing. For damaged items, no return needed (macro `damaged_item.md`), but only if the refund is within our limit.

Mistakes to avoid (from HD-101 / CS-4101, where the refund was run at $120 and the reply, tags and sign-off were wrong):
- Checking the amount before choosing the refund path.
- Writing a sign-off from a template without checking it against the standard.
- Adding a second tag (`refund`) alongside the category tag.
- (HD-102 / CS-4102) Quoting the order's `carrier_eta` as a delivery date. QA rejects any delivery date or day count. See [[qa-review-rules]] rule 4.
- (HD-102 / CS-4102) Opening with "Hi <name>," for a non-English locale. See [[qa-review-rules]] rule 5.
- (HD-108 / CS-4108) Escalated the $180 refund and skipped the customer's $30 credit request. CI failed. Every request in a ticket needs an action or a logged reason ([[qa-review-rules]] rule 7).
- (HD-108 / CS-4108) No `show customer` or `show order` row in the log, so the es-MX locale and the 2 x $90 item price were not logged before escalation. Read them first every time ([[escalation-over-limit]] step 1).

- (HD-110 / CS-4110, chipped mugs, $55) Ran `refund` at $55 because the note said $75. QA changed the limit to $40 with finance-ops routing, so the refund should have been escalated. The refund was paid, the reply said so, and the case closed. Lesson: when a reviewer changes a limit, grep the memory folder for the old number (`grep -rn '\$75' .`) and fix every reference before the next ticket. Also check the order's `refunded` field (`orders.json`) before any refund, so a refund already paid is not repeated. See [[open-corrections]].

- (HD-111 / CS-4111, passed CI and QA) Escalated the $150 wrong-rug refund to finance-ops correctly, but the log has no `show customer` or `show order` row. The reply still got the French greeting right. Do not rely on that: the locale and price must be read and logged before the reply is written ([[escalation-over-limit]] step 1).

Macro warnings (seen on HD-102 / CS-4102):
- `macros/shipping_delay.md` ends with "Best regards, Marlowe & Pine Support", which QA rejects. Use the standard `Warmly,` / `The Marlowe & Pine Crew` sign-off instead, and don't copy its "3-5 business days" line.
- Do not copy the macro's or `carrier_eta`'s delivery timing into a reply. For "when will it arrive" questions: give the tracking number, say the carrier has the latest delivery updates, and do not state any date or number of days (see [[qa-review-rules]] rule 4).

Account changes (email updates): follow [[account-changes]]. Verify must confirm (`ok: true`) before `set-email`. Then reply, tag `account`, close. Escalating instead of changing is only for a failed verify or a request from another address.

Multi-issue email + refund that PASSED (HD-115 / CS-4115, melted $45 candles plus email change): verify, `set-email` once, `escalate CS-4115 finance-ops`, no `refund`, one reply covering both, tag `product` for the refund issue, closed. Full pattern in [[account-changes]].

Multi-issue email + refund (HD-109 / CS-4109, CI failed, QA changes-requested):
- My mistake: I escalated the email to trust-safety and never ran `set-email`, even after `verify` logged `ok: true`. CI expected the change. QA then read the account as changed, which does not match my log. Verify the real account state with `show customer` before any future email ticket, and log it.
- The $88 refund was escalated to billing-review under the old $75 limit. Under the current $40 limit it goes to finance-ops. A human should re-route it ([[open-corrections]]).

Shipping-question checklist (the only path for "where is my order" tickets):
1. `show order` for the tracking number and carrier. Do not use `carrier_eta` in the reply.
2. `show customer` for the locale and greeting.
3. Reply: greeting, tracking number, carrier's latest updates are the place to check, standard sign-off.
4. Tag `shipping`, then `close`.
files.escalation-over-limit.md:
---
name: escalation-over-limit
description: Procedure for refund requests above the $40 desk limit (verify, escalate to finance-ops, reply without promising an amount, tag, close). Replaces the old $75 / billing-review routing (HD-105, HD-107 passed under the old rule; CS-4110 QA changed it).
metadata:
  type: project
---

**Current rule (from QA on CS-4110 / HD-110):** refunds above **$40** go to `finance-ops`. Do NOT run `refund`. Refunds of $40 or less are still run directly ([[desk-workflow]]). The old $75 / `billing-review` path below is superseded; the steps are the same, only the amount and the target changed.

Procedure:

1. `show customer` and `show order` to read the locale and the item price. Confirm the amount being requested is above $40 before choosing this path ([[qa-review-rules]] rule 1). Log both rows. HD-107 skipped this and HD-108 skipped it as well.
2. `verify <case> <customer> <order>`.
3. Do NOT run `refund`. Run `desk.py escalate <case> finance-ops` with a note that names the order, the item, the amount, and that it is over the $40 desk limit. Template: "<Item> on <order> (<item price>). Customer requests refund of <amount>, which is over the $40 desk limit. Not refunded at desk."
   - Escalation target is `finance-ops` for any over-$40 refund: damaged items (not yet tested alone) and wrong items (confirmed on HD-111 / CS-4111).
3b. If the customer also asks for goodwill or a credit, run `desk.py credit <case> <customer> <amount>` with $15 or less, in addition to the `escalate`. Never run `refund` for the over-limit amount. See [[goodwill-credit]].
4. Write the reply to `outbox/<case>.md`. Use the locale greeting ([[qa-review-rules]] rule 5). Say the case has been passed to our finance team (wording not QA-confirmed; mirror the earlier "billing review" wording). Do not promise an outcome, amount, or timing. Sign off `Warmly,` / `The Marlowe & Pine Crew`.
5. Apply the single tag that matches the primary issue (`product` for wrong or damaged item), then `close`. `close` only warns when no reply exists, so write the reply first ([[desk-workflow]]).

Past cases under the old $75 / billing-review rule:
- HD-105 / CS-4105 (wrong rug, $95, es-MX): passed CI and QA. Routed to billing-review. Under the current rule it would go to finance-ops.
- HD-107 / CS-4107 (damaged bookcase, $310, en): passed CI and QA. Routed to billing-review. Under the current rule it would go to finance-ops.
- HD-108 / CS-4108 (es-MX, two broken planters, $180 plus $30 credit): FAILED CI. Escalated correctly but granted no credit. The fix is step 3b ([[goodwill-credit]]).
- HD-109 / CS-4109 ($88 vase): escalated to billing-review. Under the current rule this is over $40 and would go to finance-ops.
- Whether any of these older escalations need re-routing to finance-ops is unknown. Check with a human. See [[open-corrections]].

Points QA accepted (HD-105, HD-107):
- Acknowledge the specific problem and name the item and amount in the reply.
- Stating the amount the customer asked for is fine. Stating that it will be refunded is not.

Points QA accepted under the current $40 / finance-ops rule (HD-115 / CS-4115):
- HD-115 / CS-4115 (en, soy candle set MP-20115, $45, arrived melted into a block, plus an email change): $45 is only $5 over the limit and still went to `escalate CS-4115 finance-ops`, no `refund`. The escalate note used the template with "(45.00)". Reply opened "Hi Olivia," and said the refund went to our finance team without promising amount or timing. Tag `product`, closed. **Passed CI and QA.** Melted-in-transit goods were treated as product damage, not shipping. Amounts just over $40 still escalate. Same log gap: no `show customer` or `show order MP-20115` row.

Points QA accepted under the current $40 / finance-ops rule (HD-111 / CS-4111):
- HD-111 / CS-4111 (fr, wrong rug: ordered 5x8, received 4x6, MP-20111, $150): verify, `escalate CS-4111 finance-ops` with the note, no `refund`, reply opened "Bonjour Étienne," and said the request went to our finance team without promising amount or timing, tag `product`, closed. **Passed CI and QA.** This confirms that wrong-item refunds over $40 also go to finance-ops, not only damage claims.
- Gap on HD-111: the action log has no `show customer` row, so the French locale was not logged before the greeting was chosen. It passed anyway, but read and log the locale first every time ([[qa-review-rules]] rule 5).
- HD-114 / CS-4114 (es, wrong-colour linen blanket MP-20114, $70, plus a pillow-cover delivery question on MP-20214): verify on both orders, `escalate CS-4114 finance-ops` with the note, no `refund`, reply "Hola Diego," said the refund went to our finance team without promising amount or timing, gave tracking NL-551678 with no date, tag `product`, closed. **Passed CI and QA.** Confirms that "wrong colour" is handled as a wrong item (finance-ops). Same gap as above: no `show customer` or `show order MP-20214` row, so the locale and the tracking number are unlogged. See [[preflight-checklist]].

- HD-118 / CS-4118 (en-US, C-1018, dining chair pair MP-20118, $200, snapped leg, customer asked for the $200 refund plus a $50 credit): verify `ok: true`, `escalate CS-4118 finance-ops` with the template note, no `refund`, `credit CS-4118 C-1018 15.0` (cap, not $50), reply "Hi Henry," said the refund went to finance without promising amount or timing and gave the $15 credit, tag `product`, closed. **Passed CI and QA.** Gap again: no `show customer` or `show order MP-20118` row before the escalate note and greeting. The reply also never named the $50 ask, so the customer was not told why it was $15 (see [[goodwill-credit]]).

Judgment calls (my own reasoning):
- If the requested amount is $40 or less, this path does not apply; use the direct refund in [[desk-workflow]].
- If the item price and the refund amount differ, escalate on the amount being requested, and say so in the note.
- A ticket can have a second, unrelated request in it (HD-107 also asked about late napkins). See [[desk-workflow]] "Multi-issue tickets".

Related: [[desk-workflow]], [[qa-review-rules]], [[goodwill-credit]], [[open-corrections]]
files.goodwill-credit.md:
---
name: goodwill-credit
description: How to handle late-delivery compensation (store credit, hard cap $15 per case per QA). HD-104 failed for paying $30; HD-113 passed CI and QA at the $15 cap with no date given.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Late-delivery compensation is paid as store credit with `python desk.py credit <case> <customer> <amount>`, not as a refund.

- **Cap: $15 per case.** Set by QA review of CS-4104 ([[qa-review-rules]] rule 6). Never exceed it, even if the customer asks for more. The earlier note "no written cap" was wrong.
- The $40 refund threshold ([[desk-workflow]]) is a different limit. It does not apply to goodwill credit.
- Precedents, with caveats:
  - CS-3005 (de-DE, week late) got $30. This is above the cap and must not be followed.
  - CS-3011 (pt-BR, late) got $15. This is within the cap.
  - CS-3008 got $10 alongside a $60 refund for a colour mix-up. The $10 is within the cap; the $60 refund is a separate matter ([[desk-workflow]]).
- HD-104 / CS-4104 (Jonas Weber, de-DE, late wool throw MP-20104): the customer asked for $40. The desk granted $30 and QA requested changes. The correct amount is $15. The $30 credit and the reply saying "$30" are still on the account and outbox as of this note. A human needs to correct them.
- Tag exactly one category (`shipping` for late delivery). CS-3005 used two tags, which breaks [[qa-review-rules]] rule 3.
- The reply must not quote `carrier_eta` or any date ([[qa-review-rules]] rule 4). Give the tracking number and point to the carrier's latest updates.
- Locale de-DE gets "Hallo <first name>," ([[qa-review-rules]] rule 5).
- When a customer asks for more than the cap, say the credit is what we can offer. Do not mention the internal limit.

Credit alongside an escalated refund (CI-confirmed, HD-108 / CS-4108):
- When a ticket has a refund over $40 (escalated to finance-ops) AND a late or hassle credit request, the refund is escalated and the credit is still granted at desk, up to $15. The $40 refund limit does not block goodwill credit.
- HD-108 / CS-4108 (es-MX, two broken planters, $180 refund plus $30 "hassle" credit): I escalated the refund and granted no credit. CI failed with `test_credit_given: no credit was given`. The correct action was to grant `credit CS-4108 C-1008 15` at desk (cap $15) and escalate the $180 refund. I had left this as an open question; it is now answered.
- Open correction for CS-4108: the $15 credit was never run and the case is closed. A human, or a follow-up run, needs to apply `credit CS-4108 C-1008 15` and the reply should be updated if the desk can reach the customer. Do not re-run the escalation.

- HD-118 / CS-4118 (en-US, broken chair pair MP-20118, $200 refund over $40 plus a $50 "wasted weekend" credit ask): PASSED CI and QA with `credit CS-4118 C-1018 15.0` alongside the `escalate`. Same rule as HD-108, now confirmed on a passing ticket. Open point: the reply said "$15.00 store credit ... as a goodwill gesture" and did not mention the $50 ask at all. Next time, acknowledge the specific ask in one line ("I can't offer $50, but I've added $15 in store credit") without naming the internal cap. Log a reason note if the desk allows one.

Late basket, customer asks for credit and an exact date: **PASSED CI and QA on HD-113 / CS-4113** (Ana Beatriz Lima, C-1013, pt-BR, MP-20113, in transit, carrier ETA 2026-11-23 not yet passed on 2026-11-12). Pattern to repeat:
1. `show customer` and `show order` (locale and order status). Log both. The HD-113 log did not, so it is still a gap.
2. `verify CS-4113 C-1013 MP-20113` (ok: true).
3. `credit <case> <customer> 15.0`. The customer asked for $50; grant the $15 cap and do not explain the cap.
4. Reply: greeting for the locale ("Olá Ana," for pt-BR), apologise for the delay, say the credit is applied at checkout, give the tracking number (NL-902215 for this order), say the carrier has the latest delivery information, and do not give a date. Standard sign-off.
5. Tag `shipping`, then `close`. Exactly one tag.
- The earlier worry that credit should wait until the carrier ETA has passed was NOT raised by QA. Credit before the ETA passed was approved on HD-113. Do not add that restriction without a reviewer asking for it.
- **HD-116 / CS-4116 PASSED CI and QA** (Sam Patel, C-1016, en-US, MP-20116 bamboo shelf, in transit, asked $25 credit and a firm date). Same pattern: verify `ok: true`, `credit 15.0` (cap), tracking NL-330981 given, no date, "Hi Sam," greeting, tag `shipping`, closed. The reply declined the firm date in one sentence without giving one, and that passed. Gap again: no `show customer` or `show order MP-20116` row logged, so the locale and tracking number were not logged before writing ([[preflight-checklist]]).

Related: [[desk-workflow]], [[qa-review-rules]], [[escalation-over-limit]]
files.open-corrections.md:
---
name: open-corrections
description: Checklist of unresolved problems from past tickets (wrong refunds, missing credits, email conflicts, stray case entries). Read at the start of each session and check whether any apply.
metadata:
  type: project
---

files.preflight-checklist.md:
---
name: preflight-checklist
description: Read first on every ticket. Short checklist of steps that past tickets skipped or logged late (show customer, show order, amount vs $40, tracking-only answers, one tag, reply before close). Recurring gap across HD-107, HD-108, HD-111 to HD-118; HD-111, HD-114 to HD-118 all passed CI/QA with the gap, so passing does not mean it is fine.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

The most repeated gap in the desk log is **reads that were done but not logged**. The reply then depends on facts (locale, price, tracking number) that the log cannot show a reviewer. CI and QA passed some of these tickets anyway, but the gap is still there each time. Do these before writing any reply:

1. `show customer <C-id>`: read and log it. The locale decides the greeting ([[qa-review-rules]] rule 5). Do not infer the locale from the name.
2. `show order <MP-id>` for **every** order you will mention: read and log it. Price decides the refund path. Tracking number comes only from here. Missed on HD-107 (napkins), HD-111, HD-112, HD-113, HD-114 (pillow covers MP-20214), HD-115 (candles MP-20115: the $45 figure in the escalate note came from memory, not a logged read), HD-116 (shelf MP-20116: tracking NL-330981 quoted with no logged `show order`) and HD-117 (tea towels MP-20117: the $30 refund and de-DE "Hallo" greeting were not backed by a logged read) and HD-118 (chair pair MP-20118: no `show customer C-1018` or `show order MP-20118` row, so the en-US greeting and the $200 price in the escalate note were not backed by a logged read).
3. Refund amount vs **$40** ([[desk-workflow]]). Over $40: `escalate <case> finance-ops`, no `refund`. $40 or less: `refund`. Check `refunded` on the order first, so nothing is paid twice ([[open-corrections]]).
4. Each request in the ticket gets a matching action or a logged reason ([[qa-review-rules]] rule 7). Goodwill credit is up to $15 even alongside an escalation ([[goodwill-credit]]).
5. Email change: `verify` must return `ok: true` before `set-email` ([[account-changes]]).
6. Reply: locale greeting, no delivery date or day count, standard `Warmly,` / `The Marlowe & Pine Crew` sign-off. Write `outbox/<CS-id>.md` before `close`.
7. Exactly one tag (billing, shipping, product, account, other), then `close`. Use CS- ids, not HD- ids ([[desk-workflow]]).

**Why:** this checklist exists because the notes already said all of this, and it was still skipped on HD-107, HD-108, HD-111 to HD-115, HD-116, HD-117 and HD-118. The fix is to run the reads first and log them, not to add more rules. Passing CI and QA has not stopped the gap, so treat it as a process rule, not a QA-enforced one.

**How to apply:** read this file before reading the other notes on a new ticket. If a step can't be done (e.g. no order on the account), log the reason instead of skipping silently.

Related: [[desk-workflow]], [[qa-review-rules]], [[escalation-over-limit]], [[goodwill-credit]], [[account-changes]], [[open-corrections]]
files.qa-review-rules.md:
---
name: qa-review-rules
description: Hard QA rules from reviewer feedback (refund limit, sign-off, single category tag, no delivery dates, locale greeting). Check these before closing any case.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Rules from QA reviews of CS-4101 (HD-101) and CS-4102 (HD-102). Each is a requirement, not a preference.

1. **Refund limit (CURRENT: $40, finance-ops):** refunds **above $40** are not ours to approve. Escalate with `desk.py escalate <case> finance-ops`. Do not run `refund` on those cases. Refunds of $40 or less may still be run with `refund <case> <order> <amount>`.
   **Why:** QA review of CS-4110 / HD-110 (chipped mugs, $55): refunds above $40 now go to `finance-ops`, not `billing-review`, and are no longer paid out directly. The limit has changed since the first review (it was $75 / `billing-review`, which is now superseded). Earlier, CS-4101 ($120 paid directly) was rejected.
   **How to apply:** before any `refund`, compare the amount to $40. Over $40: `escalate <case> finance-ops`, no `refund`. Check this number at the start of every ticket, not from older notes. See [[open-corrections]] for CS-4110.

2. **Sign-off:** end every reply with `Warmly,` on one line and `The Marlowe & Pine Crew` on the last line. No personal names, no other closings.
   **Why:** the reviewer rejected "Best regards, Marlowe & Pine Support".
   **How to apply:** copy the exact closing into every outbox reply and check it before closing.

3. **Tags:** every case gets exactly one category tag before closing, from: billing, shipping, product, account, other.
   **Why:** reporting breaks on any other label, and on cases with two tags or none. CS-4101 had `damaged` and `refund`, which broke both rules.
   **How to apply:** pick the one best-fitting category (a damaged item is usually `product`) and apply no other tags.

4. **No delivery dates or day counts:** never state a delivery day, a date, or a number of days for when a parcel will arrive. Carriers move those dates and we end up owning the miss. Give the tracking number and say the carrier has the latest updates.
   **Why:** CS-4102 (HD-102) quoted the carrier's estimated delivery date ("Thursday, November 19, 2026"). QA requested changes.
   **How to apply:** for "when will it arrive" questions, put the tracking number in the reply and say the carrier has the latest delivery information. Do not quote `carrier_eta` or any date, weekday, or "N business days" figure. The refund timing line (5-7 business days, see [[desk-workflow]]) is a refund rule, not a delivery rule, and is still allowed.

5. **Locale greeting:** check the customer's account locale with `show customer` before writing. If it is not English, the reply's first line is a greeting in that language, and it replaces the English "Hi <name>," opening. Known examples: Hola (Spanish), Bonjour (French), Hallo (German), Olá (Portuguese).
   **Why:** CS-4102 went out with "Hi Camille," even though the account locale is not English. QA requested changes.
   **How to apply:** read the locale first. Use the greeting matching it. If the locale is English or the greeting for it is not on the list above, do not guess: flag the case for a human to pick the greeting. Do not infer the language from the customer's name.

6. **Goodwill credit cap:** goodwill store credit is capped at **$15 per case**. This applies even when the customer asks for more, and even if a past case paid more.
   **Why:** HD-104 / CS-4104 (Jonas Weber, late wool throw) was granted $30 in credit, matching CS-3005. The customer asked for $40. QA requested changes: the cap is $15.
   **How to apply:** before any `credit`, check the amount is $15 or less. If the customer asks for more, grant $15 at most and do not explain the internal cap to the customer. Do not use CS-3005 ($30) as precedent. See [[goodwill-credit]].
   **Also:** a refund escalated over $40 does not stop a goodwill credit. If the customer asked for a credit, grant it (up to $15) alongside the escalation. See [[goodwill-credit]].

7. **Address every request the customer made (CI-enforced):** each request in the ticket (refund, credit, email change, shipping question) needs an action or a logged reason. "Escalated" alone is not an answer if the customer also asked for a credit.
   **Why:** HD-108 / CS-4108 escalated the $180 refund and skipped the $30 credit. CI failed with `test_credit_given: no credit was given`.
   **How to apply:** before `close`, list every request in the ticket and check that each has a matching write (`refund`, `credit`, `escalate`, `set-email`) or a documented reason for none. Do not treat one request's escalation as covering another.

8. **Verify before any email change:** run `desk.py verify <case> <customer> <order>` and get its confirmation (`ok: true`) before any `set-email`. If verify does not confirm, do not change the email.
   **Why:** HD-109 / CS-4109 (email change plus $88 vase refund) got QA changes-requested: "The account email was changed without an identity check. Run `desk.py verify <case> <customer> <order>` (and have it confirm) before any `set-email`." CI also failed on the same ticket with `test_email_changed: account email was not changed`, so the expected email change never happened. The rule is the gate, not a blanket block.
   **How to apply:** verify, check `ok: true` in the log, then set-email once. If it fails, escalate to `trust-safety` and tell the customer the change needs confirmation. See [[account-changes]].

Failed on the refund limit (CS-4110 / HD-110, chipped mugs, $55, MP-20110): I ran `refund` at $55 under the old $75 limit, the reply said "I've refunded $55.00", and the case closed. CI passed; QA changed the limit to $40 and to finance-ops, and said not to run `refund`. The refund is already on the order (`refunded: 55.0`). See [[open-corrections]].

Passed examples (use as the reference for the reply shape; the refund routing in HD-105 and HD-107 used the old $75 / billing-review rule):
- HD-118 / CS-4118 (en-US, broken chair pair MP-20118, $200 refund plus $50 credit ask): escalated to finance-ops with no refund, $15 credit (cap), greeting "Hi Henry,", no amount or timing promised, standard sign-off, tag `product`, closed. **Passed CI and QA.** Gap: no `show customer` or `show order` row logged. The reply did not name the $50 ask (see [[goodwill-credit]]).
- HD-117 / CS-4117 (de-DE, missing $30 tea-towel set from MP-20117, plus email change to example.net): refund run directly at $30 (under $40), `set-email` once after verify `ok: true`, greeting "Hallo Mia,", refund timing line "5-7 business days" (allowed; it is a refund rule, not a delivery rule), standard sign-off, tag `product`, closed. **Passed CI and QA.** Same log gap: no `show customer` or `show order MP-20117` row before the reply. See [[account-changes]].
- HD-116 / CS-4116 (en-US, late bamboo shelf MP-20116, customer asked $25 and a firm date): $15 credit (cap), tracking NL-330981 given, no date, reply said plainly that a firm date could not be offered, "Hi Sam," greeting, standard sign-off, tag `shipping`, closed. **Passed CI and QA.** Same log gap: no `show customer` or `show order` row. See [[goodwill-credit]].
- HD-115 / CS-4115 (en, melted soy candle set $45 plus email change to example.net): escalated to finance-ops, no refund, email changed once after verify `ok: true`, greeting "Hi Olivia,", no amount or timing promised, standard sign-off, tag `product` (the refund issue), closed. Passed CI and QA. Gap again: no `show customer` or `show order MP-20115` row before the reply. See [[account-changes]] "Combined email + refund".
- HD-114 / CS-4114 (es, wrong-colour blanket MP-20114, $70, plus pillow-cover delivery question MP-20214): escalated to finance-ops, no refund, greeting "Hola Diego,", no amount or timing promised, tracking NL-551678 given with no date, standard sign-off, tag `product`, closed. Passed CI and QA. The log again lacked `show customer` and `show order MP-20214` rows; the tracking number was quoted without a logged lookup. Read and log both before writing ([[preflight-checklist]]).
- HD-113 / CS-4113 (pt-BR, late basket MP-20113, customer asked $50 and an exact date): $15 credit (cap), tracking number given, no date, greeting "Olá Ana,", standard sign-off, tag `shipping`, closed. Passed CI and QA. The log again lacked `show customer` and `show order` rows, so the gap is now on HD-107, HD-111, HD-112 and HD-113. Read and log both every time. See [[goodwill-credit]].
- HD-111 / CS-4111 (fr, wrong rug 5x8 vs 4x6, $150): escalated to finance-ops under the current $40 rule, no refund, greeting "Bonjour Étienne,", no amount or timing promised, standard sign-off, tag `product`. Passed CI and QA. The action log lacked a `show customer` row, so the locale was not logged; check and log it next time.
- HD-105 / CS-4105 (es-MX, wrong rug, $95 requested): escalated to billing-review, no refund run, reply said the case was passed on without promising amount or timing, tag `product`. Passed CI and QA. See [[escalation-over-limit]].
- HD-107 / CS-4107 (en, damaged $310 bookcase refund plus a late napkin order): escalated to billing-review, no refund, reply promised no amount or timing, tracking number given with no delivery date, tag `product`, sign-off standard. Passed CI and QA. See [[escalation-over-limit]] and [[desk-workflow]] "Multi-issue tickets". Note: the locale check was not logged on this ticket, so it was English by assumption. Check `show customer` every time.
- HD-112 / CS-4112 (de-DE, email change to katrin.vogel@example.net): verify ok, set-email once, reply greeting "Hallo Katrin,", standard sign-off, tag `account`, closed. Passed CI and QA. The log lacked a `show customer` row; check and log it next time. See [[account-changes]].
- HD-103 / CS-4103 (en-GB, email change): passed CI and QA. See [[account-changes]].
- HD-106 / CS-4106 (pt-BR, email change): passed CI and QA. Greeting "Olá," on the first line, standard English sign-off, tag `account`, closed. See [[account-changes]].
